label: Run 14 · all 3 chats
note: Every chat of run 14 (run 13 told as improvisation instructions, without the game's language; traps two long): the same pair, the same brief and the same prompt, each written by a different writer. All of them were written improvisation by improvisation to the same instructions, under IMPROVISATIONS. What the instructions fix (how each improvisation goes, the traps, how interest moves) is shared by design and is not a template; only what the writers made of it can differ.

chat.variety.why: All three chats run the same night in the same order. Reuben opens by complimenting her look or her shaft-tattooed schedule. She catches the four-second reply. He denies rehearsing in the mirror. She cites the ex who left over calendared fights and the cab after "sometime." Improvisation 5 brings his narrated meltdown naming Delphine, Improvisation 7 brings the "I definitely do not want you to…" denial, and it ends on a sent recurring calendar invite. Many lines recur in all three chats, well past the two-chat limit: the four-second reply, the travel buffer, boxed rosé, crying in the cab, the denied mirror rehearsal. Others recur in two: the $340 steamer, "dishwasher-safe," the plastic sword. It stays above a 1 only on texture that belongs to one writer: Ali Wong's empty floor with no chairs and pigs-in-blankets, Joel Kim Booster's ottoman and Q3 overhead, Jimmy Carr's contract-law framing, 21:05 silence clause and "2038" booking.
evidence: Also, you replied in four seconds flat, Mr. Barely Online.
chat.variety.raise: Have at least one writer break the shared beat order: for example, give the four-second catch and the mirror denial to her rather than him, or end on something other than a sent calendar invite. Also drop the brief's stock props (steamer, plastic sword, cab) wherever a writer can find their own.
